newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France bans primate shipment from Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Air France bans primate shipment from Indonesia.

text.p: Air France said it had imposed an embargo on shipments of primates from Indonesia following an incident involving a baby monkey last weekend.

"Air France regulations on primates forbid the transport of baby monkeys and the shipper in Indonesia contravened on this point and broke IATA regulations. We have since decided to stop shipments from the country until further notice," a company spokesperson told Reuters.

The baby monkey was one of a shipment of primates transported aboard an Air France Cargo Boeing 747-200F flight between Jakarta and Paris from where it was transferred to another freighter bound for Chicago.
A veterinary surgeon at Charles de Gaulle airport decided to put the baby monkey to sleep following the death of its mother during the flight between Jakarta and Paris, the spokesperson said.
"The mother's cause of death was probably natural and this is currently the subject of an autopsy at the Institut Pasteur in Paris the results of which will be published in a couple of weeks."
The British Union Against Vivisection (BUAV) action group said the primates shipment, contained in 48 boxes, was destined for laboratory testing in South Carolina in the U.S..

"According to one of our sources, the shipment was due to arrive on May 30 but did not reach South Carolina until June 2 which meant they were in transit for several days," BUAV Special projects manager, Sarah Kite said.

Air France said in a statement the shipment on to the U.S. was delayed a couple of days due to a technical problem with the regular cargo aircraft. During this time the consignment was sent to the animal centre in Paris CDG where the primates received excellent professional care throughout.
On arrival in the U.S. the authorities carried out their normal checks and Air France was congratulated on their excellent condition.

"Whatever the circumstances behind this incident, we wholeheartedly condemn the transport of primates as being intrinsically inhuman and for all airlines to impose a total ban," Kite added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
